tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

Blocking: this changes the established oversized-batch contract in both participating SDKs and ingest-edge. Keep the SDK-side guard: accept batches up to and including 8,000 points, and reject only batches above 8,000 locally before any network transmission. The local error should identify the 8,000-point maximum and tell callers to split the batch; do not queue or retry the unchanged oversized request.

Ingest-edge is the backstop for older or nonconforming clients, not a partial-ingest path: after bounded decode and before acceptance/enqueue, it must reject the whole oversized batch with HTTP 413, accepted points = 0, rejected points = submitted count, and reason `oversized_batch`. Do not assume prefix acceptance or partial-result inspection; partial acceptance risks accounting gaps and duplication when callers retry/split.

Please retain/add boundary regressions proving 7,999 and 8,000 are accepted, 8,001 is rejected locally with zero sends, and server-side oversized requests (including compressed bodies) are wholly rejected with the stated accounting and no accepted work. Also verify the SDK does not retry the unchanged request. This PR's stated removal of the client limit and expectation of partial ingest violate those invariants.

Blocking: this changes the established oversized-batch contract in both participating SDKs and ingest-edge. Keep the SDK-side guard: accept batches up to and including 8,000 points, and reject only batches above 8,000 locally before any network transmission. The local error should identify the 8,000-point maximum and tell callers to split the batch; do not queue or retry the unchanged oversized request.

Ingest-edge is the backstop for older or nonconforming clients, not a partial-ingest path: after bounded decode and before acceptance/enqueue, it must reject the whole oversized batch with HTTP 413, accepted points = 0, rejected points = submitted count, and reason `oversized_batch`. Do not assume prefix acceptance or partial-result inspection; partial acceptance risks accounting gaps and duplication when callers retry/split.
